watch_items.text: **Meta settlement finalization** — the dollar figure is still unsettled across sources ($16.7B–$18B); watch for the actual signed consent decree or court filing that fixes the number and specifies which state AGs are party to it. A hard number and full state list within the next week would resolve whether this is a done deal or still being negotiated.

**Castro case appeals/Minnesota response** — watch whether Minnesota prosecutors seek any alternative route (civil action, renewed extradition request, federal charges) after the Texas ruling. Also watch for right-leaning outlets to pick up the story at all in the next 48-72 hours; continued silence would itself be notable.

**Trump's mail-in voting order** — the corpus flags this only by a garbled headline with no substantive detail. Priority item: get the actual text/scope of this order. If it restricts mail-in ballot procedures ahead of the 2026 midterms, this is a higher-significance story than currently scored and should be re-flagged.

**Iowa Senate/gubernatorial race dynamics** — watch whether other Democratic candidates in competitive states follow Turek and Sand in publicly distancing from Harris; a broader pattern would be a significant early midterm signal about the national party's brand liability.

**South Carolina general election** — watch whether Graham's opponent or outside groups directly engage the "is SC actually competitive" question WSJ raised; if Democrats pour resources into this race, it validates that framing and undercuts Trump's credit-claiming narrative.

top_cluster.headline: Meta agreed to a multibillion-dollar settlement (reported between roughly $16.7B and $18B) with a coalition of state attorneys general over claims that Facebook and Instagram were designed in ways that harmed children's and teens' mental health, and committed to new safety measures for young users.
top_cluster.left_framing: Mother Jones frames the settlement skeptically, portraying it as a reluctant, damage-control maneuver by a powerful, oligarch-controlled company seeking to shed liability and rebrand away from 'social media' rather than a sincere embrace of child safety, emphasizing corporate self-interest over genuine reform.
top_cluster.center_framing: The Hill and Axios frame the settlement as a consumer-protection and accountability victory for states, with Axios going further to cast it as a historic, tobacco-settlement-style moment that will reshape industry norms around child safety; both emphasize concrete state-led enforcement rather than corporate motive.
top_cluster.right_framing: No right-leaning or far-right outlet is included in this set, so right-of-center framing cannot be assessed from the provided sources.
top_cluster.left_omissions: Mother Jones omits the specific dollar figures used for consumer-protection framing (e.g., The Hill's 'more than $18B' investor/legal framing) and does not engage with the 'industry standard-setting' angle Axios emphasizes, focusing instead on corporate motive over structural/regulatory impact.
top_cluster.right_omissions: No right-leaning coverage is provided in this set, so it is not possible to identify what right-leaning outlets include that left-leaning coverage omits.
